story.title: Trump Calls for Action Against Senator Cotton Over Daylight Saving Bill
story.summary: Trump has urged the public to contact Senator Tom Cotton of Arkansas, accusing him of obstructing a bill aimed at making daylight saving time permanent. In a controversial move, Trump also shared Cotton's cell phone number to encourage constituents to voice their concerns directly.

related_stories.title: Bosnia Holds Elections Amid Ethnic Tensions and Pro-Russian Political Influence
related_stories.summary: Bosnia is conducting elections where approximately 3.4 million voters are selecting members for the multi-ethnic presidency, national Parliament lawmakers, and heads of institutions for the country's two entities. The elections are marked by the significant presence of a pro-Russian politician and ongoing ethnic tensions, alongside concerns regarding the stalled European Union membership bid.

related_stories.title: Cornell President Responds to Alleged Gang Rape Incident at Fraternity
related_stories.summary: Cornell University's president, Michael Kotlikoff, described the allegations of a gang rape involving a student at a fraternity house as 'deeply disturbing.' In a recent video statement, he emphasized the need for the university to improve its response to such incidents. The allegations have led to increased scrutiny of the university's handling of sexual assault cases, with the accuser, identified as Jane Doe, suing the university and several former students.

related_stories.title: Brazilians Begin Voting in Polarized Presidential Election
related_stories.summary: Voting has commenced in Brazil's 2026 presidential election, featuring incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva against Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro. The election is marked by a deeply polarized atmosphere, with polls indicating a tight race that may lead to a runoff. Approximately 160 million voters are also selecting lawmakers, senators, and governors in this significant electoral event.

related_stories.title: Latvia's Ruling Party Secures Election Victory Amid Rising Populism
related_stories.summary: In Latvia's recent parliamentary elections, Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs' United List party secured a leading position with 35.4 percent of the vote, as reported with over 99.9 percent of votes counted. The election was characterized by a notable increase in support for populist parties, reflecting a shift in the political landscape.
